Definition: a sucker; hence, a twig (of a tree felled and sprouting)
BiblicalUsage: Yoneq is a sucker, a tender shoot springing from a felled tree, and it occurs once, in the great Servant passage. Isaiah 53:2 says, "For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground." The shoot has no form or comeliness, and no beauty to draw the eye, yet it is the one God raises up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Isaiah 53:2 is the heart of this word, because God's Servant came up like a tender plant out of dry ground, with nothing to impress, and the shoot nobody noticed is the one who saves.
